subject: Geo-aware erasure requests and tenant SLA optioning
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: urgent erasure flow + geo-fallback question

Hi Vanessa,

Hope youre well. Were working through a standing request from our privacy team at NovaHealth: they want a documented, auditable erasure workflow for patient-identifiable artifacts that ensures data is removed from Redwood systems within a contractual SLA when requested. Two specific asks: 1) an option for immediate erasure (wed expect a tight SLA, e.g., <24 hours) and 2) an alternative retention-tier where we can choose a short legal-retention window (30	60 days) for investigatory reasons.

Also: what happens if the primary US region is degrading or unreachable when we submit an erasure? We need a geo-fallback guarantee or at least a documented behavior we can include in our contract. Can you provide a diagram of the end-to-end workflow and any SOC2 evidence artifacts (audit logs) that prove the steps? Ive attached our DPA redlines and the privacy teams requirement summary.

Can we schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through? Procurement (procurement@novahealth.com) is copied.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Jones
Privacy Program Manager, NovaHealth
Attachments: reqs_novah_ERG.pdf (attached by sender)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: urgent erasure flow + geo-fallback question

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the DPA redlines. Im looping in Laura (product) and Lauren (security/legal) so we can confirm compliance requirements and quick options. High-level we see two viable customer-facing options we can present to NovaHealth: 

- Option A: Immediate Erasure (Default): Tombstone + crypto-shred with a 24h SLA for the primary region. No cross-region retention, minimal audit stubs retained for up to 90 days for investigation.

- Option B: Retention Tier (Opt-In): Customer-selectable retention window (30/60/90 days) where objects are soft-deleted and can be recovered for the window. After the window, crypto-shred and purge run. Wed need to document replication behavior and backup handling for this.

Two quick clarifications we need from engineering/security: 1) is a 24h full erase SLA technically achievable across the service surface (including replicas/backups), and 2) how do we handle a region-unavailable scenario — will requests queue to the next healthy replica or fail-over?

I can do the meeting tomorrow 1pm PT — does that work for everyone?

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-05T12:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: urgent erasure flow + geo-fallback question

Thanks for pulling this together. Technical notes from infra/serving side:

1) Erasure stages we recommend (staged erase):
   - Tombstone (immediate logical delete) 
   - Crypto-shred (rotate/delete encryption keys so ciphertext is unrecoverable) 
   - Physical/Blob purge (background job that deletes objects from store)

2) Cross-region replication: if we replicate synchronously, to guarantee erasure across replicas we must coordinate the crypto-shred across regions. If primary region is degraded, we can queue the request and failover to a read replica to accept the erase request, but that introduces complexity for consistent truncation of replication logs.

3) Backups: long-lived snapshots are the hard part. To meet a strict <24h SLA for "complete" erasure (including backups), we either need backup tombstone awareness (retention-aware snapshots) or define that backups are immutable and excluded from the SLA (we can provide attestations for when backups roll off).

4) Implementation effort: rough estimate: 3 sprint baseline to add per-tenant retention flagging + workflow orchestration (tombstone/crypto-shred/purge) + audit log plumbing. Add 2 more sprints for cross-region coordination and backup integration.

Ill attach a quick diagram of the proposed staged-erase flow and an impact matrix for replication/backups.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Attachments: erasure_workflow_diagram.png

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-05T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: urgent erasure flow + geo-fallback question

Couple of infra points to add: 

- Object store lifecycle hooks: we need a purge queue integrated into blob storage with per-tenant priorities so urgent erases bubble to the front. Thats ~2 sprint infra work to ensure safe deletion ordering and idempotency.
- Replication pause/coordination: during crypto-shred we must pause cross-region replication of affected objects to avoid resurrecting data. That requires a short lease/lock mechanism (tech debt).
- Audit/event CDC: to provide SOC2-quality evidence we need an immutable audit stream (Kafka topic with retention) and a signed attestation bundle generator. This is low-latency but requires ops runbook.

Cost/ops impact: higher S3 egress and metadata churn for retention tiers; also additional CPU/time for crypto operations. Recommend gating the paid SLA tier to offset costs.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-05T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: urgent erasure flow + geo-fallback question

Legal/compliance input:

- Some healthcare regulators require an auditable trail for erasure requests; we should keep at least an immutable record of the request, the timeline, and the attestation that crypto-shred/purge occurred. That record can be retained longer than the object payloads themselves (90 days is a reasonable default).
- DPA redlines: NovaHealth is asking for explicit language that we will not resume replication of deleted data and that we will provide an attestation within X days. Legal prefers 7 calendar days for attestation delivery.
- Suggest offering a "Certified Erasure" add-on: includes prioritized purge queue, cross-region coordination, and signed attestation for a fee. This both addresses risk and creates a monetizable feature.

Ill review the DPA redlines attached and mark clauses we should seek concession on.

-Lauren Bishop
Director, Security & Compliance
